statement: A disclosure scan over the net diff of a range cannot see exposure that was added and removed inside it: the closed-name guard reported 0 hits from the parent of one pull request's merge to the merge of the later scrub, while the first pull request alone carried 22 hits in three files, not only the one record the defect report was about. Git history keeps that exposure public regardless. Rule: run a disclosure guard per pull request (or per commit) as it lands, never only over a range afterwards, and when auditing a past leak, scan each merge on its own before trusting a net-zero range result as the scope of the defect.

A guard that withholds the matched text but prints the file path still leaks when the path itself holds the name: a new file added at a closed-name path would have been named in public CI logs by the very check that caught it. Rule: in a disclosure guard, treat every printed field (file path, branch name, commit subject) as candidate text and withhold any that matches, and test that the failure output for a path hit does not contain the token.
